AO No.118 of 2017
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J. e 
Mr. B.S. Bisht, Advocate holding 
brief of Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for the 
appellant. 
Issue notices to the respondents 
on delay condonation application, if 
any. 
Steps be taken within a week. 
Call the LCR. 
List this matter after the service 
is affected. 
Subject to deposit of Rs.15 Lakhs 
of the total awarded amount, adjusting 
the compulsory statutory amount, 
within six weeks from today before the 
Tribunal concerned, recovery against 
the appellant shall remain stayed. 
Stay Application (CLMA No. 1928 
of 2017) stands disposed of. 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)

17.06.2022 AO No. 118 of 2017
With

Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Tarun Pande, Advocate, holding 
brief of Mr. Prabhat Pande, Advocate, for the 
appellant/Insurance Company.
Mr. Nikhil Singhal, Advocate, for the 
respondents.
These are the two connected Appeals 
from Orders, which are arising out of the same 
accident. 
Connected AO No. 647/2016, has been 
preferred by the claimants for enhancement of 
the amount of compensation, as it has been 
determined on 14.09.2016 by the learned Motor 
Accidents Claims Tribunal, in its proceedings 
held by way of MACP Case No. 161 of 2013, 
Smt. Reena Srivastava & Others Vs. Smt. 
Savita & Others. It was was admitted on 
30.11.2016. Notices were issued to respondent 
Nos. 1 to 3. But, there is an office report, that 
respondent Nos. 1 & 2, have not yet been served 
with the notices.
Hence, while allowing the Urgency 
Application (IA/15302/2022), filed in AO No. 
118/2017, directing the appellants of AO No. 
647/2016, to take fresh steps for effecting 
services on the unserved respondent Nos. 1 & 2. 
Steps would be taken by the appellant
of AO No. 647/2016 within a period of one 
week from today.
List these matters after the service of 
notices on the unserved respondent Nos. 1 & 2.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 17.06.2022 Mahinder/
